name: client

scripts.//vercel-build: Compatibility shim for a Vercel project whose Root Directory is still `client/`: Vercel then runs `npm run --workspace=client vercel-build` from client/, and its absence fails the deploy with 'Missing script: vercel-build'. Hop back to the repo root and drive the real build from there — the server workspace and the root dependencies must be installed and compiled too, and a client-scoped install skips both. Note this only produces the static site: with Root Directory at `client/`, the repo-root vercel.json is never read and `api/index.mjs` is outside the deployment root, so no API function is created. Point Root Directory at the repo root and this script goes unused.
scripts.vercel-build: cd .. && npm run install:all && npm run build

//optionalDependencies: Rollup ships its native binary as a per-platform optional dep, and npm records only the host platform's in package-lock.json (npm/cli#4828). A lockfile generated on Windows therefore breaks Linux CI with 'Cannot find module @rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu'. Declaring the Linux binaries explicitly puts them in the lock; npm skips them on other platforms because each declares its own os/cpu.
